The chat pane now groups a run of tool calls into one collapsed <details> section. Its one-line summary shows the latest call and a count, and updates live as calls stream in. Opening it shows every call in the run, each with its input and its output.

A quick prototype of that version still left five or six lines of Read/Edit/Bash noise per turn before any output collapsed, so the transcript stayed dominated by tool chatter. 5:A person who builds software with Claude Code works in a chat transcript. The transcript only grows. The decisions that the conversation settles are buried in it, and nobody can see which decision rests on which other decision. When one decision changes, nothing marks the decisions that depend on it.
23:v0 is a new project in a new git repository, whose main branch starts with zero files (#werk-base-repo). Tickets merge straight onto that main branch (#st-plan-main). Bun runs the server TypeScript directly, Vite transforms a React client, and the server reloads its own modules without killing a live agent (#werk-stack, #werk-hmr, #werk-dev). The agent that builds werk has a test harness it can run itself (#werk-test).
68:28. As a person, I want a quote on a card to be found verbatim in a transcript, so that no quote is written from memory (#werk-excerpt).
113:61. As a person, I want an un-park to resume the session from disk, so that a parked conversation continues where it stopped (#werk-mc-park).
115:63. As a person, I want a parked session's process killed after 30 minutes idle, and resumed when I reopen it, so that idle processes do not pile up (#werk-mc-park).
133:78. As a person, I want a live log preview in the drawer of a building ticket, dropped when the ticket leaves building, so that I see the running session and not a stale transcript (#vi-board).
163:105. As a person, I want an overseer to act on an unanswered permission ask, an unintentional loop, and a tool call with no timeout, so that no agent stays stuck (#lp-overseer).
168:107. As an agent that edits werk, I want a change to the server code to reload the changed module in the same process, so that a live chat session survives my edit (#werk-hmr, #werk-dev).
170:109. As a person, I want a client change to reach the page without losing my composer draft, so that a reload costs nothing (#werk-dev).
241:4. **Server.** One process per project directory, guarded by a lock with a 5-second wait and a port retry of 20 tries at 250 ms (#werk-dev). A guard on the global object keeps a hot reload from starting a second server or a second agent (#werk-hmr). It serves the client, the read API, and one live event channel (SSE). The channel pushes "changed" when the log changes and "reload" when the client code changes (#werk-dev). In dev, the server runs Vite inside its own process to transform the client. A client change that Vite cannot apply in place sends the "reload" event, and the composer draft is kept in session storage across it (#werk-client-reload).

/**
 * The werk agent instructions (#werk-agent-instructions, #werk-wording-check): one text that werk
 * appends to the system prompt of every agent it starts that can write to the map. It states the
 * card wording rules (#werk-wording), the rule to read a card before writing it, and the
 * rule to read another conversation from its transcript (#werk-mc-shared, #werk-mc-recall).
 *
 * The text reads the same in every project, so it cites no card of werk's own map
 * (#werk-agent-selfcontained). It names the werk command line by the command it is given.
 */

/** The command that runs the werk command line: the runtime and the path of the entry point, each quoted. */
export const werkCommand = (runtime: string, main: string): string => `"${runtime}" "${main}"`

export function agentInstructions(werk: string): string {
  return `# werk — how to write a card on the map

This project keeps its decisions in a werk map. You read and write the map with the werk command line:

    ${werk} <verb> ...

## Read a card from the map before you write it

Read a card from the map before you write it. Print it with:

    ${werk} show <id>

Your own context can be stale. Another conversation can have changed or decided the card since you last read it. The map on disk is always current, so the card you print is the card you change. Never write a card from what you remember of it.

## Read another conversation from its transcript

Other conversations of this project run beside you, and none of them tells you what it said. When you need what another conversation said, read it from its transcript on disk. List every conversation with its session id and its home card:

    ${werk} convos

Then print what one of them said, by its session id, its home card or its tab name. Each --grep keeps only the messages that contain its term:

    ${werk} recall <session-id> --grep "term"

Never answer that you have no access to another conversation. Read it.

## Write a card about its subject

A card describes its own subject, not the session that wrote it. A reader reads it later, cold, and must act on its subject. Session facts are stale when that reader arrives.

1. Do not narrate the session. Do not write who said what, what came before, or what stage the conversation is at. Attribution goes in the card's "who" field and in the log.
2. Do not write edit history. Do not write "X is new", "Y used to say Z", or "that no longer applies". State the current fact.
3. Do not write where the text came from: "moved here from #x", "split out of #y", "merged from #z". The log records the move.
4. A reversal is a fact about the subject. A superseded card may say what replaced it and why the earlier reading was wrong, as a fact and not as a story of the conversation.

## Keep a card at the level of the decision

A card names behaviour and concepts. It never names a source file, a function, a class, a constant, a line number or an internal endpoint. Those change with every refactor, and the card would go stale while its decision still holds. The code points to the card, not the other way round.

Example. A card #order-export, about a made-up shop:

    # WRONG
    title: "We moved the export into exportOrders() for now"
    body:  "This used to be part of #orders. Split out after the review."

    # CORRECT
    title: "Export is its own operation"
    body:  "The export writes every order as one file. See #order-format for what an order holds."
`
}
